newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parliament delays foreign borrowing vote.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parliament delays foreign borrowing vote.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament, debating the 1997 draft budget in its second reading on Tuesday, put off until later this week a vote limiting foreign borrowing in 1997.
The draft budget, nearly six months late, proposed a $4.3 billion borrowing limit.
Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov told deputies about $1.4 billion in foreign credits would be used to cover the budget deficit and the balance would be implemented in government programmes.
Parliament asked the government to provide full details on the programmes before voting on the matter in the third and final reading, scheduled for Thursday.
Once Ukraine passes the budget, it will take a key step towards qualifying for a three-year, $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) credit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

Mityukov said Ukraine was expecting a $1.1 billion credit from the World Bank for deficit financing and a $230 million credit for small business development, $165 million in credits from the European Union and Japan, and $100 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
Anticipated loans also included a first tranche of $900 million from the IMF's EFF, and $600 million in trade credits with various countries.
He added Ukraine expected to receive about $500 million "at minimum" from its first foreign bond issues planned for September.
Mityukov said Ukraine's external debt totalled $8.6 billion.

Parliamentary deputies earlier approved revenues of 22.39 billion hryvnias ($12.1 billion) and expenditures of 28.12 billion hryvnias, and that 3.33 billion hryvnias of the projected defict would be covered using domestic sources of cash and 2.4 billion hryvnias from foreign credits.

It rejected a proposal by the budget and finance committee to use only funds from the Treasury bill market to cover the deficit on the domestic side, allowing the possibility that the central bank would cover part of the deficit.
